name: Resonant Microwave Denial System RMDS-4 'Crowdbreaker'
description:
The RMDS-4 is a directed-energy area denial platform that projects a diverging cone of millimeter-wave microwave radiation, tuned to the 94 GHz frequency band at which water molecules in the subcutaneous layer of human skin absorb energy most efficiently. The effect on exposed targets is an immediate, overwhelming burning sensation across all exposed skin surfaces — described universally by subjects as being 'cooked from the outside in.' The sensation is intense enough to trigger involuntary flight response in virtually all subjects within seconds, regardless of training or psychological preparation.

Developed by Tessera Corponation's non-lethal security division, the RMDS-4 is explicitly designed not to cause permanent injury under standard exposure protocols. At rated power and exposure times under four seconds, the weapon produces no lasting tissue damage — the burning sensation ceases within seconds of leaving the beam. This has made it extraordinarily attractive to corporate security operations that need to control crowds or breach occupied spaces without generating the liability of lethal force. However, the weapon's power output can be adjusted beyond factory defaults, and modified units operating above rated parameters cause severe epidermal burns, corneal damage, and at extended high-power exposure, fatal hyperthermia.

The RMDS-4 is mounted on a shoulder-rig platform with a 120-degree horizontal sweep and a 30-degree vertical arc, controlled by a handle-mounted targeting interface. The emitter head is recognizable by its distinctive hexagonal radiating array — a design that has become visually synonymous with corporate crowd control in GLMZ's visual culture, appearing in protest art and propaganda with striking frequency.
specifications:
platform: Shoulder-rig mounted, single-operator
weight: 11.4kg (rig and emitter)
power source: Tessera Type-6 high-capacity cell, 40 minutes continuous at rated power
frequency: 94 GHz primary, 77 GHz secondary (penetrates light cover)
effective range: 0–50m (primary denial), 50–120m (reduced intensity)
beam spread: 120-degree horizontal sweep, 30-degree vertical arc
rated exposure limit: 4 seconds at standard power (non-injurious)
override capability: Factory-limited; modified units documented at 340% rated output
tactical_use: Standard deployment places the RMDS-4 operator behind a defensive line, using the wide beam spread to push crowds or groups away from a defined perimeter. In breach scenarios, it is used to clear rooms before entry — the beam passes through standard interior walls at reduced intensity, causing enough discomfort to drive occupants toward exits where entry teams are positioned. Corporate security teams typically deploy one RMDS-4 per four-person unit as a force multiplier. The weapon's main tactical vulnerability is its shoulder-rig format — the operator is relatively immobile during sustained use, and the emitter array is bulky enough to be a targeting priority for hostile snipers.
cultural_context: The Crowdbreaker is one of the most politically loaded weapons in GLMZ. Its official designation as a non-lethal system has allowed corporations to deploy it against labor protests, housing disputes, and unauthorized gatherings with legal impunity. The hexagonal emitter array has become a symbol of corporate repression in activist communities — it appears spray-painted on walls, incorporated into protest banners, and tattooed on the bodies of people who survived its use. The existence of modified high-output units is an open secret that Tessera Corponation disputes aggressively, and several journalists who documented RMDS-4 burn injuries in excess of rated parameters have subsequently faced significant legal pressure.
known_users: Municipal security forces in corporate-administered districts
Underground modification specialists (modified units resold to private buyers)
story_hooks: A protest group has acquired a modified RMDS-4 running at 340% output and is planning to use it — not for crowd control, but as retaliation against a corporate event. The players are asked to stop them, but the client turns out to be the corporation that deployed RMDS-4s against the protesters' community in the first place.

A journalist has documented fatal hyperthermia cases from an RMDS-4 incident and needs the evidence extracted from a Tessera-controlled server before the legal team buries it. The data is real, the risk is real, and Tessera knows someone is looking.

A modified RMDS-4 is being auctioned through a black market channel. Several buyers want it badly enough to kill for it. The players are either protecting the auction, robbing it, or have been hired to ensure a specific buyer doesn't win.

physical_description.visual_profile: A brutalist shoulder-mounted energy platform dominated by a prominent hexagonal emitter array. The silhouette is aggressive and asymmetrical—a wide, flat radiator head mounted on a reinforced articulated arm extending from a heavily padded backplate. Reads as industrial crowd-control equipment; unmistakable and deliberately imposing.
physical_description.dimensions: Emitter head: 34cm diameter (hexagonal), 8cm depth. Articulated arm span: 62cm fully extended. Backplate: 48cm × 38cm. Total shoulder-rig footprint when mounted: 78cm wide × 45cm tall × 22cm deep.
physical_description.weight_description: Hefty and anchoring. The 11.4kg load sits low and distributed across shoulder and hip straps, but the forward-mounted emitter creates leverage that demands active postural compensation. Operators describe it as 'wearing a small vehicle.'
physical_description.primary_material: Aluminum composite frame with steel reinforcement at articulation points. Emitter array housing: pressure-cast titanium alloy rated for thermal stress. Backplate: carbon-fiber composite.
physical_description.finish: Matte tactical black on frame and backplate. The hexagonal emitter array is bare brushed titanium with high-polish facing—the radiator surface gleams in direct light, creating a distinctive contrast. Stress points show worn chrome plating.
physical_description.color_scheme: Matte black primary, brushed titanium silver on emitter face. Accent: Tessera Media Group corporate blue stripe running down the backplate articulation spine.
physical_description.grip_texture: Handle-mounted targeting interface features rubberized pistol-grip with aggressive texturing for gloved operation. Secondary stabilization grips are wrapped with non-slip paracord. All contact surfaces are slightly tacky to the touch—engineered for sweat resistance.
distinctive_features: Hexagonal emitter array with visible individual radiator elements arranged in concentric rings
Horizontal sweep mechanism with visible servo motors and articulated linkage
Backlit LCD targeting reticle on handle interface (faintly glowing in darkness)
Heat-stress scarring visible on titanium emitter face—micro-discoloration patterns from repeated use
Tessera corporate logo stamped into backplate (3cm, chrome relief)
Safety interlocks with redundant manual override switches positioned along left side of rig
Thermal bleed vents cut into lower frame section, often with scorching marks
Asymmetrical power cell housing on right hip—bulky rectangular module with cable routing
Targeting laser diode (red, 635nm) visible as small aperture on upper emitter housing
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: Tessera Media Group logo (5cm stamped relief) on backplate. Serial plate mounted on left arm articulation: white text on black anodized aluminum (8cm × 3cm). Individual unit designation engraved near power-cell housing. Factory specifications plate affixed below emitter array.
physical_description.condition_typical: Well-maintained equipment shows light carbon scoring on emitter face and heat-stress discoloration on the titanium array. Field-deployed units often display impact marks on the backplate, worn grip texture, and corroded fasteners. Heavy-use platforms show permanent warping of thermal vents and micro-fractures radiating from stress points. Modified ('hot-rodded') units exhibit crude welding repairs, crude heat shielding, and visible jury-rigging of power regulators.
